concepts.def: The surface where one material ends and a different material begins, for example air and glass or air and a brick wall. When a wave arrives at a boundary it can be reflected, absorbed or transmitted, and in most real cases all three happen at once in differing proportions.

The process in which a wave arriving at a boundary is sent back into the material it came from, rather than passing into the second material. Reflection happens at a boundary between any two different materials, not only at mirrors.
Reflection from a smooth surface, such as a plane mirror or still water. Parallel incident rays stay parallel after reflecting, so a clear image is formed.

Reflection from a rough surface, such as paper or a painted wall. The surface behaves as many tiny facets pointing in different directions, so parallel incident rays are scattered and no image is seen. The law of reflection still holds at every point.
The process in which the energy carried by a wave is transferred into the energy stores of the material at the boundary, usually the thermal energy store, so the wave itself does not continue.

The process in which a wave passes through the boundary and continues to travel inside the second material. A transmitted wave usually changes speed, and if it meets the boundary at an angle to the normal it also changes direction.

The change in direction of a transmitted wave at a boundary, caused by the change in the speed of the wave as it enters a different material. A wave travelling along the normal changes speed but does not change direction.

The construction line drawn at right angles to the surface at the point where the ray meets it, shown dashed in a ray diagram. Angles of incidence, reflection and refraction are all measured from the normal.
The angle between the incident ray and the normal at the point of incidence.
The angle between the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence. For any surface, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

A drawing showing the surface, the dashed normal at the point of incidence, the incident ray and the reflected ray, each drawn as a straight line with an arrow giving the direction of travel, with both angles marked from the normal.

What happens to a wave depends on the wave and on the two materials meeting at the interface. A matt black surface absorbs most visible light, a silvered surface reflects most of it, clear glass transmits most of it, and soft furnishings absorb much of the sound reaching them.

An investigation in two parts: shining a ray of light from a ray box at different types of surface and observing and measuring the reflected ray, then shining a ray into different transparent substances, such as a rectangular glass block or a perspex block, and tracing the refracted ray.

The technique of drawing round the block or surface, marking the incident and emerging rays with two pencil crosses set well apart, then removing the block and joining the crosses with a ruler so that the path inside the block can be drawn and the angles measured from the normal.

mcqs.q: A sound wave travelling through the air reaches a thick concrete wall. Which statement best describes reflection at this boundary?
options: Some of the sound is sent back into the air it originally came from
Reflection cannot occur here, as concrete is not polished
All of the sound must pass on into the concrete and travel through
The wall turns the sound into a wave of a much higher frequency
mcqs.explain: Reflection at a boundary sends part of the wave back into the first material, and air and concrete are two different materials.

mcqs.q: A lamp lights a plane mirror and a sheet of white paper equally. A clear image is seen in the mirror but not in the paper. Why is this?
options: The rough paper scatters rays and so breaks the law of reflection
The paper absorbs every ray of light that arrives at it
The smooth mirror keeps parallel rays parallel when they reflect
Paper transmits light, but a mirror is unable to transmit
mcqs.explain: Specular reflection at a smooth surface preserves the pattern of the rays so an image forms, whereas the rough paper scatters them.

mcqs.q: A radio wave meets a thick metal sheet and is absorbed. What happens to the energy that the wave was carrying?
options: It is destroyed, so less energy exists than there was before
It is transferred to the thermal energy store of the metal
It is stored inside the wave until that wave is set free again
It becomes a reflected wave of exactly the same frequency
mcqs.explain: Absorption transfers the energy carried by the wave into the energy stores of the material, most often the thermal store.

mcqs.q: Light from a street lamp shines on a clean window and carries on into the room beyond. Which word describes what the light has done at the glass?
options: The light has been absorbed by glass
The light has been reflected away
The light has been fully destroyed
The light has been transmitted
mcqs.explain: Transmission is a wave passing through the boundary and continuing to travel inside the second material.

mcqs.q: A narrow ray of light travels through air and meets the flat surface of a glass block. Which statement about this boundary is correct?
options: All the light is transmitted, because the glass is transparent
All the light is absorbed, since the glass warms up a little
Some light is transmitted into the glass and some is reflected back
None of the light gets in until the angle reaches ninety degrees
mcqs.explain: In general all three effects occur together, and a faint reflected ray is visible alongside the much brighter transmitted one.

mcqs.q: You are drawing a ray diagram for light reflecting from a plane mirror. From which line is the angle of incidence measured?
options: From the normal, drawn at right angles to the mirror surface
From the mirror surface, at the point where the ray lands on it
From the reflected ray, measuring back to the incident ray
From the bottom edge of the paper the diagram sits on
mcqs.explain: Angles of incidence and reflection are always measured between the ray and the normal at the point of incidence.

mcqs.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection, and from where is it measured?
options: 60°, measured from the normal, since they total 90°
30°, measured from the surface of the mirror
60°, measured from the mirror surface, not the normal
30°, measured from the normal on its other side
mcqs.explain: The law of reflection gives angle of reflection = angle of incidence, with both angles measured from the normal.

mcqs.q: Which feature must appear in a correctly drawn ray diagram showing reflection at a plane mirror?
options: A dashed normal drawn along the mirror surface
Arrows on the rays to show the direction
The image marked in front of the mirror surface
An angle of reflection larger than incidence
mcqs.explain: Rays are drawn as straight lines carrying arrows, so the diagram shows which way the light is travelling.

mcqs.q: A matt black metal plate and a shiny silver metal plate are left side by side in bright sunlight. Why does the black plate become hotter?
options: It reflects more of the light, and reflection is what warms a surface
Black surfaces transmit the sunlight straight through into the metal
The silver plate absorbs the light but re-emits all of it at once
It absorbs more of the light, transferring that energy to its thermal store
mcqs.explain: Absorption at the interface transfers the energy of the wave into the material and raises its temperature; reflected energy leaves again.

mcqs.q: Heavy fabric curtains are drawn across a window facing a busy road, and the room becomes noticeably quieter. Which effect best explains this?
options: The curtain reflects all the sound waves straight back
The soft fabric absorbs much of the sound that reaches it
The curtain lowers the frequency below what ears detect
The curtain slows the sound so it arrives too late to hear
mcqs.explain: Soft porous materials absorb sound, transferring the energy of the wave to their thermal energy store, so less is transmitted into the room.

mcqs.q: In Required practical activity 9 a ray box is aimed at a plane mirror, then at gloss card, then at matt card. Which quantity must be kept the same throughout?
options: The angle of incidence of the ray from the box
The kind of surface that the ray box is aimed at
The angle of reflection read off the protractor
The sharpness of the reflected ray on paper
mcqs.explain: The type of surface is the independent variable, so the angle of incidence is the control variable and must be held constant.

mcqs.q: In Required practical activity 9 a ray of light is shone from air into a rectangular glass block, meeting the surface at an angle to the normal. What is seen as the ray enters the block?
options: It bends away from the normal
It carries straight on, unbent
It bends towards the normal
It only bends when it leaves
mcqs.explain: Light slows on entering glass, so a ray meeting the surface at an angle to the normal is refracted towards the normal.
